intervals.note: See experiment:cupid interval note; no confirmed physical-construction start date sourced in this session. `start` (2025) is the earliest dated CUPID collaboration paper found, a lower bound not a true start date.
intervals.quote: CUPID will profit of the established CUORE cryogenic infrastructure, and deploy ~1500 Li2MoO4 crystals in place of the TeO2 ones.

name: CUPID detector
notes: Placed at site:lngs-hall-a (dangling reference: owned by the 'facilities' lead, not yet created).

Verification note (2026-09-17, src:0vbb-verify-*): the cited source confirms LNGS generally, not the Hall A designation specifically. CUPID is planned to reuse the CUORE cryostat, which is in Hall A, but no directly fetched source in this session states 'Hall A' for CUPID verbatim; confidence on the placement remains 'uncertain' for this reason as well as the unconfirmed construction timeline.

placements.note: site:lngs-hall-a is owned by the 'facilities' Wave 3 lead and does not exist yet in this repository (dangling reference). The cited source states the general LNGS location, not the Hall A designation; see record-level verification note.
placements.quote: Laboratori Nazionali del Gran Sasso (LNGS) in the Abruzzo region of central Italy

isotope_mass.quote: a planned 240 kg isotope mass of 100Mo

summary.plain: About 1500 crystals of lithium molybdate, designed to both flash light and register heat when a particle hits them, planned to fill CUORE's existing refrigerator under the Gran Sasso mountain.
summary.technical: Planned array of ~1500 Li2MoO4 scintillating bolometers targeting 100Mo (Qbb = 3034 keV), to be installed in the existing CUORE cryostat at LNGS.

technology.quote: Lithium molybdate crystals, described as a scintillating material with a particle-dependent light yield
